title: I Let the Roommate Keep the No-Overnight-Guests Clause He Wrote

parts.text: I read the house agreement Nolan printed after I moved in: no overnight guests without seventy-two hours notice and a yes from both. I was twenty-three. I followed it. Nolan's boyfriend slept over four nights a week and used my oat milk. I photographed the agreement, the shoes in the hall, and the oat milk level. Sunday I asked for seventy-two hours notice for his next stay. Nolan said the clause was to keep me from having strangers. Then he changed the Wi-Fi password while I was at work and left a note: guests don't get the network.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He locked me out of Wi-Fi with a rule he wrote against my guests, not his.

social.video_title: He wrote a guest clause that only pointed at me — Part 1/2
social.description: Oat milk, hallway shoes, and a seventy-two hour rule with a boyfriend already asleep. Then the Wi-Fi died. Would you have moved out?

parts.text: I restored the Wi-Fi from the router sticker, which was in the lease packet under my name too. I emailed Nolan the clause and a calendar: his boyfriend could stay if he posted seventy-two hours and replaced the oat milk. Nolan called me petty. I called me literate. The boyfriend started going to his own place on weeknights. The shoes left. I bought new oat milk and labeled it. The agreement stayed on the fridge. Both names were on it. Both names still are.
